question: Toilet paper is cheapest per roll in big packs and on promotion. Which American households use those savings least?
answer: Low-income households. Orhun and Palazzolo followed the toilet paper bought by tens of thousands of American families over several years. The poorest bought small packs and missed sales, paying a few per cent more per sheet than bulk and sale buying would cost, even with cheaper brands. Bulk takes spare cash and cupboard space.
move: A discount you need money to reach is not open to everyone.
trap: Assuming the rich skip bargains because they can afford to.
source: Orhun & Palazzolo, Journal of Marketing Research, 2019
reference: Orhun & Palazzolo, Frugality Is Hard to Afford, Journal of Marketing Research, 2019
